title: Concurrent strength and endurance training effects on running economy in master endurance runners
authors: Piacentini MF, De Ioannon G, Comotto S, Spedicato A, Vernillo G, La Torre A
journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
population: Regularly training master marathon runners (about 43-45 years); 16 participants randomized to maximal strength training (n=6, 44.2 years), resistance training (n=5, 44.8 years) or control (n=5, 43.2 years)
findings: The maximal strength training group improved 1RM by 16.34% and running economy by 6.17% at marathon pace (p < 0.05).
The resistance training and control groups showed no significant changes (p > 0.05).
Anthropometric data were unchanged in all groups.
Authors call it a preliminary study and suggest rate of force development may be crucial for the economy improvement.
limitations: Very small groups (5-6 per arm), self-described preliminary; intervention length and frequency not stated in the abstract; marathon-pace economy only; no performance outcome; sex mix not stated in the abstract.
implications: For runners aged about 40-50, heavy low-rep work is justified on the same basis as for younger runners; do not default masters to light high-rep circuits only.
Treat 6.17% as a hypothesis-level number; keep masters rules aligned with the general rules.

verification.notes: Crossref and Europe PMC re-fetched; group ages and p-values added from abstract.
